patches.name: ep1-rhodes
patches.notes: THE patch — Brian Eno's E.PIANO 1 preset. ROM cartridge slot A-11. Replaced Rhodes/Wurli on virtually every 80s ballad. Velocity-sensitive: soft plays bell-like, hard plays glassy + bright. Range a1-a5 (full 88 if you have it). Used in: Phil Collins 'One More Night', Whitney Houston 'Greatest Love of All', Chicago 'Hard to Say I'm Sorry', ~10,000 charting tracks 1984-1992. THE most-used digital preset of all time.

patches.name: bass1-slap
patches.notes: DX BASS 1 — the slap bass that defined 80s funk-pop. Bright attack, percussive, velocity-controls brightness. Range a1-a3. Used in: Phil Collins, Genesis, Whitney Houston, Stevie Wonder, every 80s ballad with no real bassist.

patches.name: tub-bells
patches.notes: TUB BELLS — the iconic FM bell that became 'the Twin Peaks sound' / Tubular Bells. Soft mallet hits with long sustain. Range c2-c6. Used in: Twin Peaks theme (Badalamenti), Angelo, ambient productions, Boards of Canada-adjacent.

patches.name: marimba
patches.notes: DX MARIMBA — wooden percussion tone. Bright attack, quick decay. Range c2-c6. Used in: Tears for Fears 'Everybody Wants to Rule the World' lead line, jazz-fusion productions.

patches.name: harpsichord
patches.notes: HARPSICH 1 — bright, plucky harpsichord. Used in: 80s symphonic-pop ballads, soundtrack work. Range c2-c6.

patches.name: brass1
patches.notes: BRASS 1 — bright FM brass stab. Synthy, not realistic, but iconic. Range c2-c6. Used in: 80s pop horn-sections, A-ha, Howard Jones.

patches.name: strings
patches.notes: STRINGS 1 — FM string ensemble. Synthetic warmth, slow attack. Range c2-c6. Used in: 80s ballad pads under E.PIANO 1, all kinds of soft-rock layering.

patches.name: pipes
patches.notes: PIPES 1 — the chime/whistle that became the iconic 'plastic flute'. Used in: A-ha 'Take On Me' instrumental sections, mid-80s synth-pop. Range c3-c6.

patches.name: tenor-sax
patches.notes: TENOR SAX — FM sax patch, breathy attack. Synthetic but iconic. Range c2-c5. Used in: 80s smooth jazz, Kenny G-era productions, sax solos when you couldn't book a player.

patches.name: wurly-dx
patches.notes: WURLY — DX7's take on the Wurlitzer EP sound. Mellower than EP1, more 'soulful'. Range a1-a5. Used in: Neo-soul productions where they want EP character but with DX glassiness.

patches.name: log-drum
patches.notes: LOG DRUM — woody percussive patch, useful as one-shot percussion or melodic hits. Range c2-c5. Used in: tribal-pop, hand-drum simulations, Peter Gabriel-era productions.

patches.name: fm-pad
patches.notes: FM PAD — slow-attack pad with FM 'shimmer' on top. Range c2-c5. Used in: ambient productions, soundtracks, atmospheric layering. Less iconic but a workhorse.

patches.name: fretless-bass
patches.notes: FRETLESS BS — DX7's fretless bass impression. Smooth attack with subtle vibrato. Range a1-a3. Used in: smooth jazz, R&B ballads, Wayman Tisdale era.
